title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
why_read: A solid systems/graphics paper showing how to make expensive neural avatar animation nearly 1000x cheaper by approximating it with simple linear blendshapes, with real mobile performance numbers.
analysis: This paper tackles a real bottleneck in 3D Gaussian avatar rendering: the per-frame neural network inference needed to animate photorealistic avatars is too slow for real-time use on weaker devices. The authors show that this expensive neural step can often be approximated by a simple linear combination of precomputed 'blendshapes', similar to classic facial animation techniques, learned via block-local PCA. Their distillation method, GALA, swaps the heavy neural decoder for a lightweight coefficient predictor and linear blend, cutting CPU cost by up to three orders of magnitude while keeping most visual quality, reaching 60fps on mobile. This is a genuinely useful systems contribution for anyone building real-time avatar or telepresence applications.
